text:
Marathon Petroleum bounced 2.8% today after sliding 6.97% over the past two weeks, reversing some recent losses. The stock's recovery appears tied to renewed optimism about refining profitability: U.S. oil is trading at $103 per barrel while global oil sits at $123, creating a wide spread that favors refiners who buy cheap domestic crude and sell into global markets. Refineries are running at 92.8% capacity and fuel inventories remain relatively tight—gasoline storage at 209 million barrels and diesel at 103 million—conditions that support stronger margins on fuel output.

There's also a timing factor in the air: Marathon announced a leadership change and company update on October 29th, the same day CNBC reported that Big Oil earnings guidance would matter most to investors going forward. With refining conditions currently favorable and the company signaling a fresh strategic direction, traders may be repositioning ahead of upcoming earnings and commentary.
